This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via run_action (literal, a string literal in TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS))_
- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via run_action (literal, a string literal in TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS))_

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via run_action (literal, a string literal in TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via run_action (literal, a string literal in TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via run_action (literal, a string literal in TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 919a781b90ec8a4510fe1089123d693e92443951` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eea03485f92a6c938e6f2de9ecbed3a5a39538aa` — the merge of head `f3352a3ddfc2b44e46c2b6731b7964b1e164e8ca` into base `919a781b90ec8a4510fe1089123d693e92443951`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eea03485f92a6c938e6f2de9ecbed3a5a39538aa && git checkout eea03485f92a6c938e6f2de9ecbed3a5a39538aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 919a781b90ec8a4510fe1089123d693e92443951 f3352a3ddfc2b44e46c2b6731b7964b1e164e8ca && git checkout -B drift-repro 919a781b90ec8a4510fe1089123d693e92443951 && git merge --no-ff f3352a3ddfc2b44e46c2b6731b7964b1e164e8ca

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 919a781b90ec8a4510fe1089123d693e92443951
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 919a781b90ec8a4510fe1089123d693e92443951` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `975dd7d0ec3a0edf88eb56a230788f475f808488`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.test.ts + packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/tool-call-interceptor.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/README.md, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (cited, read, not reviewed)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no published schema or governed path in the four-file diff). Inputs: card #32767 body and its four comments, the PR body, file list and net diff against merge-base `ba321c27`, and the check-runs on this head.

Check-runs on this head when this record was written: concluded `success` on Build Core, every `Lint ·` job, Type Check · source gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs affected by code changes. STILL RUNNING, no verdict yet: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger; `Lint & Repo Gates` queued. The mcp suite and the two families the dev could not measure locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`) therefore have no gate verdict on this head yet. The SDK is not installed in the reviewing tree, so the shape of its `_registeredTools` registry (object keyed by name, `enabled` flag) is taken from the wire pins, which Test Core has not concluded.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept-set of `prompts/list` and `prompts/get` on `handleHttpRequest`: narrowed to skills whose every `tools` entry the request's server serves. RIGHT against the card's Expected (first shape), and the mechanism holds: `registerSkillPrompts` is installed before `wireBridgeTools` and `registerAuthoringTools` (`mcp-server-runtime.ts` 2596 onward), but `servedToolNames(server)` is read inside each handler, after every family registered and before `server.connect`, so it is the list `tools/list` answers.
2. A withheld skill is filtered before the face list and before `lookupSkillPrompt`, so `prompts/get` answers the plain `-32602` not-found with no `data`. RIGHT, and pinned.
3. `listSkillPrompts(bridge)` keeps its signature and stays unfiltered; the long-lived stdio server (`mcp-server-runtime.ts` 2292 to 2369) calls it and `registerPrompt`, never `registerSkillPrompts`. RIGHT: the runtime's own stdio surface is unchanged.
4. Public surface: no new entry export (`index.ts` 71 to 72 unchanged; `skillBindingServed` is module-only). RIGHT. But the behaviour of the EXPORTED `registerSkillPrompts` changed for every caller, not only for `handleHttpRequest`. See F3.
5. Fail-open when the SDK registry is unreadable (`servedToolNames` returns `undefined`, every skill offered). RIGHT as a degradation, same private read as `tool-call-interceptor.ts` 249; it restores the pre-change answer and the data-only pin goes red on it.
6. `Metadata-protocol: none`. WRONG. See ② and F1.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: RIGHT. No exported type, signature or accepted input widens; a connection is answered fewer prompts. BREAKING banner, remedy and ADR-0087 disposition are all present in the changeset.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` with `@objectstack/mcp: patch`: WRONG, must-fix (F1). `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` 504 defines `semantic` as "the meaning or default of an authorable key changes", level `minor`. `SkillSchema.tools` is an authorable key whose published meaning in this distribution is "authored for cloud and inert here" (`skill.zod.ts` class JSDoc and the `tools` JSDoc and its `.describe()` text). After this diff the same key decides whether the skill's `instructions` are served on the HTTP MCP door: an author who adds or removes one name in `tools` changes what a client is offered. The dev's own report says so ("the HTTP MCP door reads it as an offering gate"). Precedent on `main`: runtime-only changes to how authored metadata is served are declared `semantic` and ship `minor` (`.changeset/30062-declared-override-mapping-removal-remedies.md`). The changeset's ADR-0087 comment sentence "`SkillSchema.tools` keeps its shape and meaning" is true of the shape only. Owed: `Metadata-protocol: semantic` on the PR body and the changeset, `@objectstack/mcp: minor`, and that sentence corrected. The ADR-0087 disposition itself (not-required, nothing at rest moves) stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

**(a) `action_NAME` counts as served when `run_action` is served.** The reading is RIGHT in direction, and its implementation has one gap.
- Spec: `skill.zod.ts` says of `tools`, "Over MCP ... an AI-exposed Action is already reachable as `action_NAME` through `list_actions` / `run_action`", and `PLATFORM_TOOL_FAMILY_PREFIXES` is exactly `['action_']`. Runtime: `registerActionTools` (`mcp-http-tools.ts` 2857 onward) registers `list_actions`, `run_action` and optionally `resume_run` behind `actions:execute`, and no native family registers a tool under the `action_` prefix. Under the strict reading every action-bound skill would be withheld on every native connection, including one that can run the action, which defeats the card (offer the playbook where the connection can run it). Option A is accepted. `list_actions` alone correctly does not open the door (pinned).
- Accepted deviation, not a finding against A: the door is grant-level. It does not check that the named action exists, is AI-exposed, or is runnable by this caller; that would cost a `listActions` read per prompt request, and `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` already checks the reference at authoring time.
- Gap, should-fix (F2): "MCP never registers `action_NAME` tools" holds for the native families only. `registerAuthoringTools` "registers what it is handed" from the host registry, and the exported `registerSkillPrompts` runs on any host server; a server that literally lists `action_resolve_case` without `run_action` gets `false`, because `bindingEntryServed` returns `served.has(door)` at line 213 before the literal and wildcard match. That contradicts the changeset's own first rule ("a plain name is served when `tools/list` lists it") and the spec's "plain names match a tool with that exact name".

**(b) The `SkillSchema.tools` JSDoc ("cloud-runtime-only", "inert here").** Yes, it is now false for the open framework's HTTP MCP door, and it is wider than the one JSDoc: the class JSDoc ("`instructions` served everywhere ... any connected MCP client can `prompts/list` / `prompts/get` a skill", "these keys are authored for cloud and inert here"), the `tools` JSDoc and its `.describe()` string ("bound by the cloud agent runtime only", which ships in the generated schema and reference), `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` 242 ("Everywhere"), and `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` 383. A skill written exactly like the spec's own checked example (four `stack.tools` names no runtime serves) is now offered on no HTTP MCP connection. Ruling: NOT a must-fix inside this PR. `packages/spec` and `skills/**` are outside the claim's file surface and would change this PR's review face; the card's Expected authorises the narrowing itself. It IS owed as a follow-up card, should-fix (F4): filed and named in this PR's body before landing, and carried in the same release as this changeset, so the published spec and the published behaviour do not disagree in a release. The `skills/**` part of that card takes the contract tier.

**Dev out-of-scope notes.** stdio not filtered: accepted, the card measured the HTTP door, and judgment 3 confirms the runtime's stdio path is untouched (but see F3 for hosts). cloud#4419 proxy drop after the next pin move: carrier noted, nothing owed here.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it takes a declared capability away at the consumer ("`instructions` served everywhere") and does so on purpose, on the card's Expected, with a BREAKING banner and a remedy. It does not make an existing spec refusal real; the spec says the opposite today, which is why F1 and F4 exist. The design itself holds: filter by the connection's own tool registry, read at answer time, withheld equals unknown.

Attempts to break it, and what held:
- Order of registration, empty grant, disabled tools, non-string entries, a non-array `tools`, a row with no `tools`: all behave as documented. An empty registry is an empty set, not `undefined`, so a server serving no tool withholds every tool-bound skill; consistent.
- Wildcards: `create_*` is served by `create_record` alone on a `data:write` connection without the authoring family, so `object_drafting`-style skills pass on any one match. Inherent to "any tool it matches" and stated in the changeset; accepted.
- Tools MCP serves under no grant (`visualize_data`, `search_knowledge`, `query_data`, `aggregate_data`, and any `stack.tools` name): skills binding them are withheld on every connection unless a host injects them. Consistent with the rule; it makes the PR body's line that a fully granted connection is exactly as before true only for skills whose tools that connection lists. Covered by F4's wording.

Findings:

- **F1, must-fix** (`.changeset/32767-mcp-skill-prompts-served-tools.md`, PR body): `Metadata-protocol: none` / `patch` should be `semantic` / `minor`; correct the "keeps its shape and meaning" sentence. Reasoning in ②. Prose faces only.
- **F2, should-fix** (`packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts` 209 to 219): let an `action_` entry be served by a literal or wildcard match in `served` OR by the door, instead of by the door alone; add the unit pin (`action_resolve_case` listed, `run_action` absent, expect `true`). Moves the head; delta review owed.
- **F3, should-fix** (changeset body, PR body): the reach is understated. The filter lives in the exported `registerSkillPrompts`, which `packages/mcp/README.md` 262 to 291 documents for hosts driving their own `McpServer`, with a stdio example. Such a host is narrowed too, by its own server's registry. "The stdio transport is unchanged" and "narrowing of the HTTP prompt surface" are true of `MCPServerRuntime` only; say that the exported helper now filters by the server it is installed on. Prose faces only.
- **F4, should-fix** (follow-up card, outside this diff): the spec and docs prose named in ③(b). File it, name it in the PR body, same release.
- **F5, nit** (`skill-prompts.ts` 206): `TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS` hand-copies `'action_'` from `PLATFORM_TOOL_FAMILY_PREFIXES`; a family added to the spec would be read strictly here with no test noticing. A pin that every spec family prefix has a door would close it. Follow-up or accepted deviation.
- **F6, nit** (`skill-prompts.ts` 185 to 196, `lookupSkillPrompt`): filtering before the face list means a duplicate face (ADR-0150 D6, "refused at every get, never one of them served") is refused on a connection serving both skills and serves the one remaining skill on a connection where the other is withheld; likewise a bare name two packages hold. Defensible (withheld equals unknown, and the refusal would otherwise name a withheld skill), but unstated and unpinned. Accepted deviation, or one sentence in the module doc on a later prose pass.
- **F7, nit** (`skill-prompts.ts` 240 to 241): "go red on such an SDK in both directions" overstates; on an unreadable registry the two data-only pins go red and the two CONTROL pins stay green.

Tests: the six pins exercise the wire path with real grants and an injected authoring family, each negative paired with a CONTROL, and the three ablations in the PR body each turned a named pin red. The shared-fixture change (`listActions` / `runAction` on `makeDataBridge`) is needed and correctly explained. Missing pin: F2's case.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-hngw2d`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cz8zK9vJDPeeVKJ4XP`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cb72dff9bee109ae84093908f1da36231221c3d7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.test.ts + packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (cited, read, not reviewed)

Delta review of the FAIL record 6838062944 (head `975dd7d0`). Inputs: the one-commit delta `975dd7d0..cb72dff9` (the changeset, `skill-prompts.ts`, `skill-prompts.test.ts`; `mcp-server-runtime.ts` untouched since the reviewed head), the PR body as now stored, the changeset, follow-up card #32885, and the check-runs on this head. The earlier record's judgments on everything the delta does not touch stand.

Check-runs on this head when this record was written: concluded `success` on Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates and every `Lint ·` job, TypeScript Type Check and all four `Type Check ·` jobs (workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger, source gates), PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Test Core 4/8 and 8/8. Check Changeset has two runs: the first concluded `failure` because it read the PR body before the seat's patch (its log: "declares ... metadata-protocol `none`, and it introduces a changeset entry graded `minor`"); the re-run after the body patch concluded `success`, and it is the newer one. STILL RUNNING, no verdict yet: Test Core 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8. The two new pins and the F2 logic therefore have no concluded test verdict on this head unless the mcp suite sits in shard 4 or 8; landing waits for all eight.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `bindingEntryServed` (`skill-prompts.ts` 210 to 225): a wildcard is served by any listed name with its stem, a plain name by the listed tool of that name, and only then is a family entry served by its door. RIGHT. Every case of the old order gives the same answer except the one F2 named (family member listed by name, door absent), which moves from `false` to `true`. A non-family entry with no match still falls through to `false`.
2. `TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS` gains `export` at module level. RIGHT and not a public-surface change: `index.ts` names its re-exports from `skill-prompts.js` one by one and does not name it.
3. Changeset level `minor` with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, on both the changeset and the PR body. RIGHT.
4. No other accept-set or surface moves in the delta.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` are line-initial and identical on the PR body and the changeset; `@objectstack/mcp: minor` is the level `semantic` owes (`clause2-line.mjs` 504). The BREAKING banner, the remedy and the ADR-0087 not-required disposition are kept, and the disposition sentence now says the key keeps its shape while its meaning on the MCP prompt surface changes. Matches what the diff publishes. The re-run of Check Changeset agrees.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) action door: closed by the F2 fix; option A stands, now as "that literal or wildcard match, or else `run_action`". The grant-level reach of the door is recorded in the PR body as an accepted deviation.
- (b) spec and docs prose: #32885 is filed, open, `Blocked-by: #32767`, names the spec JSDoc and `.describe()` text, `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` and `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, states same-release order and the contract tier for the `skills/**` part; the PR body carries `Skills-docs: follow-up #32885` and the changeset names it. Answered.

### ④ Design judgment

Each earlier finding, checked in the tree at this head:

- **F1 (was must-fix): FIXED.** See ②.
- **F2 (was should-fix): FIXED.** Logic as in ① item 1. New pin "a family member a host server lists by name is served by that tool, without the family door" covers plain, wildcard and a negative (`action_close_case` listed, `action_resolve_case` bound, expect `false`). The earlier door pin still holds under the new order (`run_action` alone serves both entries; `list_actions` alone serves neither).
- **F3 (was should-fix): FIXED.** The changeset title, body and BREAKING paragraph name the exported `registerSkillPrompts`, every server it is installed on, hosts driving their own `McpServer` (stdio included), and that `MCPServerRuntime.bridgePrompts` is unchanged (the method exists at `mcp-server-runtime.ts` 2173 and does not call the helper). It also states that a skill binding a tool no MCP family serves is offered on no connection. The PR body says the same.
- **F4 (was should-fix): FIXED** by #32885, see ③(b).
- **F5 (was nit): FIXED.** Pin "every platform tool family the spec declares has its MCP door here" reads `PLATFORM_TOOL_FAMILY_PREFIXES` from `@objectstack/spec/system`; the constant's doc names the pin.
- **F6 (was nit): ACCEPTED DEVIATION**, stated in the PR body's Acceptance notes with its reason.
- **F7 (was nit): FIXED.** The comment now says the two data-only pins go red and their CONTROL pins stay green.

Regression pass over the delta: none found. The reordering cannot turn a previously served entry unserved (the door check is still reached whenever the match fails), and the only newly served case is the intended one.

New findings, nits only:

- **N1, nit** (PR body): "`skillBindingServed` is exported from the module for its unit pins only" should also name `TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS`, now exported from the module for the same reason.
- **N2, nit** (card #32885 text): its What and Expected still say "HTTP MCP door" and "an `action_NAME` entry is served through `run_action`"; the landed rule is the reach of `registerSkillPrompts` and "by a tool of that name, or else through `run_action`". Whoever takes #32885 should write the prose from the changeset, not from the card's summary.

Both are prose outside the reviewed tree; neither moves the head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f3352a3ddfc2b44e46c2b6731b7964b1e164e8ca`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.test.ts + packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts, packages/mcp/src/types.ts (cited, read, not reviewed)

Merge delta on the PASS record 6838468174 (head `cb72dff9`). This head is one merge commit of `origin/main` (parents `cb72dff9` and `919a781b`, which carries PR #32902) and nothing else. The earlier records' judgments stand; only what the merge could change is judged here.

Check-runs on this head when this record was written: concluded `success` on Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates and every `Lint ·` job, Type Check · consumer gates, debt ledger and source gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Test Core 7/8 and 8/8. STILL RUNNING, no verdict yet: Test Core 1/8 to 6/8 and Type Check · workspace. Landing waits for them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. The PR's own diff is unchanged by the merge. RIGHT: the net diff against the new merge base `919a781b` and the net diff reviewed at `cb72dff9` against `ba321c27` have the same stable patch-id (`52fa5774`), over the same four files (changeset, `mcp-server-runtime.ts` +3 -1, `skill-prompts.test.ts`, `skill-prompts.ts`).
